description:
Known for his thunderous shot and physical play, defenseman Shea Weber unleashed a signature blast during Game 3 of the 2016 Second Round against the San Jose Sharks. When the puck bounced out to the high slot, Weber stepped into it and fired a bar-and-in rocket for the eventual game-winning goal. A dominant presence on the blue line throughout his NHL career, Weber also excelled internationally, earning two Olympic gold medals (2010 and 2014) and a World Championship title in 2007. His remarkable achievements were honored with his induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2024.

description:
A player who excelled in every facet of the game, Nicklas Lidstrom achieved success at all levels, winning an IIHF World Championship gold medal, the 2006 Olympic gold medal, and four Stanley Cup championships. The year 2002 was particularly exceptional for Lidstrom, as he captured both the Conn Smythe and Norris Trophies while leading the Detroit Red Wings to their third Stanley Cup in six years. In Game 2 of that Final, Lidstrom delivered a clutch performance, hammering a one-timer past the goaltender late in the third period for the game-winning goal, sending the home crowd into a frenzy. A seven-time Norris Trophy winner, Lidstrom remains the all-time leader among Swedish-born NHL defensemen in goals, assists, and points, along with an astonishing +450 career plus/minus rating.

description:
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2011, Mark Howe made history as the youngest player to win an Olympic medal in ice hockey, securing a Silver Medal at just 16 years old during the 1972 Olympics. In the 1985 Stanley Cup Playoffs, Howe delivered a memorable overtime goal against the New York Rangers with his signature wrist shot, breaking the Flyers' playoff win drought that had stretched since 1982. The Flyers would later reach the Stanley Cup Final that year but fell to the Edmonton Oilers. Howe, whose No. 2 jersey is honored in the Flyers' rafters, concluded his career with an impressive +400 plus-minus rating and 28 shorthanded goals, the most ever by a defenseman in NHL history.

description:
Jeremy Roenick was one of only four U.S.-born players in NHL history to surpass 500 career goals when he was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame as part of the 2024 Class. One memorable moment came in a game against the Rangers, where he toe-dragged a defender and deked past the goalie for a highlight-reel goal. Across 20 NHL seasons with five teams, Roenick tallied 1,216 points, cementing his legacy as one of the game's most dynamic players.

description:
No Finnish-born goalie has played more NHL games (683), won more games (369), or recorded more shutouts (60) than Pekka Rinne. Facing the Blackhawks in Chicago with a two-goal lead, Rinne launched a perfect shot from behind his goal line, sending the puck into the empty net. The remarkable moment was capped off as his teammates mobbed him in celebration.

description:
Ron Francis was one of the most consistent and productive players in NHL history. Across an incredible 23-season career, he amassed 1,798 points, ranking 5th all-time. Renowned for his elite playmaking and defensive skills, Francis recorded 1,249 assists—second only to Wayne Gretzky (1,963) in NHL history. A two-time Stanley Cup champion with the Pittsburgh Penguins (1991, 1992), he also earned the Selke Trophy (1994-95) and the Lady Byng Trophy three times (1994-95, 1997-98, 2001-02). Spending most his career with the Hartford Whalers/Carolina Hurricanes and Pittsburgh Penguins, Francis retired as one of the most accomplished and respected centers in the game. In his final postseason with Carolina, the team captain delivered a memorable moment, scoring the overtime winner in Game 1 of the 2002 Stanley Cup Final—his last playoff goal. His remarkable legacy was solidified with his induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2007.

description:
Joe Nieuwendyk was an elite two-way center and a proven winner during his 20-season NHL career. A three-time Stanley Cup champion with three different teams (Calgary Flames, Dallas Stars and New Jersey Devils), he scored 564 goals. Known for his leadership and clutch performances, Nieuwendyk won the Conn Smythe Trophy in 1999 and was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2011. While with the Devils, he scored his 500th career goal in spectacular fashion, evading a defenseman and cutting across the crease to tuck the puck around the goalie. Later that season, he capped off his illustrious career by capturing his third and final Stanley Cup.

Teemu Selanne, a four-time Olympic medalist (silver in 2006; bronze in 1998, 2010 and 2014), enjoyed a remarkable NHL career. A Calder Trophy and Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy winner, Selanne amassed 684 career goals, with 457 of those scored during his time with the Anaheim Ducks (a franchise record). During the second of his back-to-back 50-goal seasons with Anaheim, Selanne dazzled with a stunning goal against the Calgary Flames, deftly maneuvering around a defender and scoring a beautiful backhander. A Hockey Hall of Famer, Selanne spent 15 of his 21 NHL seasons with Anaheim, where he also claimed the Bill Masterton Trophy in 2005-06 and secured a Stanley Cup in 2007.

description:
Henrik Zetterberg, a cornerstone of the Detroit Red Wings for all 15 of his NHL seasons, built a legacy as one of hockey’s most respected stars. A 2008 Stanley Cup champion, he earned the Conn Smythe Trophy that year, becoming the second Swedish-born player to win the award. Zetterberg also found success on the international stage, capturing both an Olympic gold medal and a World Championship title in 2006. His knack for clutch performances was on full display during the 2013 Stanley Cup Playoffs when, facing the Anaheim Ducks, he scored the Game 6 overtime winner in front of the home Detroit crowd, forcing a Conference Quarterfinals Game 7 that the Red Wings would go on to win.

description:
Saku Koivu is a proven winner in international hockey, having earned a Gold Medal at the 1995 IIHF World Championships, a Silver Medal at the 2006 Olympics, and Bronze Medals at the 1994, 1998 and 2010 Olympics. In the NHL, the beloved former captain of the Montreal Canadiens faced a challenging 2001-02 season, undergoing cancer treatment that limited him to just three regular-season games. Despite the setback, Koivu made a remarkable comeback in the playoffs. In Game 3 of the first round against the Boston Bruins, the Canadiens' historic rivals, he scored the game-winning goal in front of a roaring home crowd. Koivu's courage and resilience earned him the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy that season.
